question: Approve the design and enter implementation? Approving accepts D1 (anchors: observer law at 91fae734, dispatch-record law at the state tip on the day the workflow turns on), D2 (push trigger on the named state branch only, no schedule), D3 (option A: GitHub's failed-run notice, zero FO words; flips to the 19-word pr_watch line before merge if your notice does not arrive) and D4 (two laws in v1), each as recommended, with FO's change: v1 runs the CI workflow only on this repository's state branch, and adopters opt in after its minutes are measured. It also accepts the batch-1 implementation order (names-check-before-dispatch lands before extension-instruction-reaches-dispatch, which edits the same dispatch_records.py function; the other three run in parallel), and is the grant for the implementation worker to push a branch and open a Draft PR.

artifacts.summary: Design: package laws file plus scripts/laws_check.py running observer_check.py and dispatch_records.py over committed state history after a per-law anchor; a GitHub Actions workflow on pushes to the state branch; detects, cannot prevent. Absorbs none of the other four. Measured at e73634e6: observer law 0 of 9 events violate after its anchor; dispatch-record law 12 of 68 records violate after 49da5ddb (7 in the open journey-server-host-pilot), hence the anchor at turn-on. Unverified until implementation (AC-8, AC-9): whether GitHub runs a workflow committed on the state branch, whether state init, gate prepare and merge guard --rework leave .github/ alone, and whether the failed-run notice reaches you. FO's change: this branch saw up to 1024 pushes in 30 days and private adopters pay CI minutes (unmeasured), so v1 stays on this public repository.
